messages.author: 158ee0f539b93c4d
messages.subject: Interpreting RSF results
parts:
Hi Chris and all,

I'm struggling to interpret some of my RSF results with manatees and wondering if you could help me.

One variable (freshwater springs) has significant results (0.85, 95% CI [0.06, 1.65]) for the population mean but when I isolate one subarea of my study, the same variable is not significant (0.04, 95% CI [-0.72, 0.80]). This doesn't make sense as this predictor was only used for the animais in this subarea, because we only have freshwater springs in part of the species distribution.

Is there any possible statical explanation for this?

Thank you!

Iran Normande

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Interpreting RSF results
parts:
Hi Iran,

It is possible that beta[freshwater] is correlated to another variable beta[correlate] in the population, and beta[correlate] is not well resolved in the subpopulation, but it is well resolved in the population, and through that correlation beta[freshwater] can be resolved in the population.

You can check by comparing the CI widths and inspecting cov2cor(MEAN$POV), which are the population parameter correlations.

Best,
Chris
